terms.definition: An element that is shiny, malleable, and an excellent conductor of heat and electricity.
terms.function: Makes up about 80% of the elements and powers everything from wiring to bridges to cookware.
terms.whereItIs: The left side and middle of the periodic table.
terms.whyItMatters: Metals are the backbone of the modern world and a doorway into understanding electricity and bonding.

terms.definition: The shiny, reflective quality of a metal's surface.
terms.function: Lets polished metals gleam and reflects light strongly.
terms.whereItIs: The bright highlight on the ingot's surface.
terms.whyItMatters: Luster is one of the fastest ways to recognize a metal by eye.

terms.definition: The loose outer electrons of metal atoms that wander freely between atoms.
terms.function: Carry electric current and heat through the metal, which is why metals conduct so well.
terms.whereItIs: The drifting dots inside the ingot in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Free electrons are the physical cause of every famous metal property.

terms.definition: A positive ion formed when an atom loses electrons.
terms.function: Metals tend to become cations in reactions, which lets them bond with negative nonmetal ions.
terms.whereItIs: Formed whenever a metal atom gives away its loose outer electrons.
terms.whyItMatters: Metal cations and nonmetal anions are the two halves of every ionic bond.
